newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia peso falls as centbank buys dollars.
newsitem.headline: Colombia peso falls as centbank buys dollars.

text.p: Colombia's peso continued its downward trend, falling 0.35 pesos to 998.68 to the dollar, as the central bank stepped in to prop up the greenback.
"There were a lot of dollars flowing into the markets today and very little real demand," one interbank trader said.
Traders said the central bank began buying dollars when the peso hit 998.68, the upper limit of the bank's daily floating exchange rate band.
"A large bank sold the central bank $18 million in two $9 million deals," the trader added.

The central bank declined to confirm the level of its intervention in the market. The fall of the peso in recent days has been due to the central bank's crawling peg devaluation program and not a reflection of genuine demand from buyers for dollars.
"We'll finish the year like this with a lot of dollars and a lot of pesos," another dealer said.
Interbank traders reported trades worth a total of $135.2 million. The peso hit an intraday low of 998.90 and closed at the day's high of 998.6.
